note: Ps107 great thanksgiving, 4 'cried to the LORD' vignettes (43v, 200 spans). Read by CHAR-ARC. A call v1-3 (GIVE-THANKS). Vig1 wanderers v4-9 (WANDERED, HUNGRY/THIRSTY/SOUL FAINTED -> CRIED -> THANK; the LONGING/HUNGRY SOUL satisfied). Vig2 prisoners v10-16 (AFFLICTION because REBELLED/SPURNED, HEARTS bowed -> CRIED -> THANK). Vig3 sick fools v17-22 (FOOLS through SINFUL-WAYS/INIQUITIES, SUFFERED-AFFLICTION, LOATHED food -> CRIED -> healed -> THANKSGIVING/TELL/JOY). Vig4 sailors v23-32 (SAW deeds, COURAGE MELTED, WITS' end -> CRIED -> GLAD/DESIRED-haven -> EXTOL/PRAISE). Coda v33-43 (EVIL inhabitants; HUNGRY dwell; BROUGHT-LOW/SORROW; princes WANDER; NEEDY raised; UPRIGHT GLAD, WICKEDNESS silenced; WISE ATTEND/CONSIDER his love). God's deliver/satisfy/heal/still-the-storm/reversals = qualifiers; desert/irons/waves/agriculture imagery = standalone.

dims.v: v1: 'Oh GIVE THANKS (yadah) to the LORD, for he is good' - the opening call, the frame of the whole thanksgiving.
v4: 'Some WANDERED (taah) in desert wastes, finding no way to a city' - the lost, homeless in the wilderness, the first plight.
paired with thirst and the fainting soul
v5: 'HUNGRY (raeb) and thirsty, their soul fainted within them' - the starving wanderers, need pressing on the body.
v5: 'hungry and THIRSTY (tsame)' - the parched wanderers, thirst added to hunger.
v5: 'their SOUL (nephesh) fainted within them' - the inmost self failing under hunger and thirst.
v5: 'their soul FAINTED (ataph) within them' - the swooning of the wanderers, life ebbing in the waste.
v6: 'Then they CRIED (tsaaq) to the LORD in their trouble' - the cry of the lost, the refrain-turn from distress to rescue.
the LORD for his steadfast love
v8: 'Let them THANK (yadah) the LORD for his steadfast love' - the summons to gratitude, the refrain's response to deliverance.
v9: 'For he satisfies the LONGING (shaqaq) soul' - the yearning self God fills, desire met with good.
v9: 'he satisfies the longing SOUL (nephesh)' - the inmost self God contents.
paired with the hungry soul filled
v9: 'and the HUNGRY (raeb) soul he fills with good things' - the starving self God feeds.
v9: 'the hungry SOUL (nephesh) he fills with good things' - the inmost self satisfied by God.
v10: 'prisoners in AFFLICTION (oni) and in irons' - the bound and suffering, the second plight.
v11: 'for they had REBELLED (marah) against the words of God' - the defiance that earned the chains, affliction as the fruit of rebellion.
the counsel of the Most High
v11: 'and SPURNED (naats) the counsel of the Most High' - the contempt for God's counsel behind the imprisonment.
paired with falling with none to help
v12: 'So he bowed their HEARTS (leb) down with hard labour' - the inner self broken by toil, pride humbled in the pit.
v13: 'Then they CRIED (zaaq) to the LORD in their trouble' - the cry of the bound, the refrain-turn to rescue.
the LORD for his steadfast love
v15: 'Let them THANK (yadah) the LORD for his steadfast love' - the summons to gratitude for the burst bonds.
paired with their sinful ways and iniquities
v17: 'Some were FOOLS (evil) through their sinful ways' - the foolish whose sin brought sickness, the third plight.
v17: 'fools through their SINFUL WAYS (pesha)' - the transgressions that made them fools and brought affliction.
v17: 'and because of their INIQUITIES (avon) suffered affliction' - the guilt that issued in sickness.
v17: 'because of their iniquities SUFFERED AFFLICTION (anah)' - the sickness endured as sin's consequence.
v18: 'their SOUL (nephesh) loathed any kind of food' - the inmost self sickened, appetite failing at death's door.
paired with the soul near death
v18: 'their soul LOATHED (taab) any kind of food' - the revulsion at food of the mortally sick, life recoiling.
v19: 'Then they CRIED (zaaq) to the LORD in their trouble' - the cry of the sick, the refrain-turn to healing.
the LORD for his steadfast love
v21: 'Let them THANK (yadah) the LORD for his steadfast love' - the summons to gratitude for the sent word that healed.
paired with telling his deeds in joy
v22: 'And let them offer sacrifices of THANKSGIVING (todah)' - the thank-offering of the healed, gratitude enacted.
v22: 'and TELL (saphar) of his deeds in songs of joy!' - the recounting of God's works, testimony sung.
v22: 'tell of his deeds in songs of JOY (rinnah)!' - the gladness of the healed voiced in song.
the deeds of the LORD in the deep
paired with the storm that follows
v24: 'they SAW (raah) the deeds of the LORD, his wondrous works in the deep' - the sailors' witness of God's power on the sea.
v26: 'their COURAGE (nephesh) melted away in their evil plight' - the inmost self unnerved, heart failing as the ship heaved.
v26: 'their courage MELTED (mug) away' - the dissolving of the sailors' nerve before the storm.
v27: 'and were at their WITS' (chokmah) end' - the sailors' skill exhausted, seamanship undone by the sea.
v28: 'Then they CRIED (tsaaq) to the LORD in their trouble' - the cry of the storm-tossed, the refrain-turn to calm.
v30: 'Then they were GLAD (samach) that the waters were quiet' - the relief of the sailors at the stilled sea.
v30: 'and he brought them to their DESIRED (chaphets) haven' - the longed-for harbour, the goal of the storm-tossed.
the LORD for his steadfast love
v31: 'Let them THANK (yadah) the LORD for his steadfast love' - the summons to gratitude for the calmed storm.
paired with praising in the assembly
v32: 'Let them EXTOL (rum) him in the congregation of the people' - the public praise of the delivered, gratitude among the assembly.
God in the assembly of elders
v32: 'and PRAISE (halal) him in the assembly of the elders' - the worship of the delivered before the elders.
paired with the land turned to waste
v34: 'a fruitful land into a salty waste, because of the EVIL (raa) of its inhabitants' - the wickedness that turns fruitfulness to salt.
paired with being settled in a city
v36: 'And there he lets the HUNGRY (raeb) dwell' - the needy God settles, hunger answered with a home.
v39: 'When they are diminished and BROUGHT LOW (shachach)' - the abasement of the people through affliction.
v39: 'through oppression, evil, and SORROW (yagon)' - the grief of the afflicted, the low estate of the humbled.
paired with the contempt poured on them
v40: 'and makes them WANDER (taah) in trackless wastes' - the princes brought low, the mighty made to wander like the lost.
v41: 'but he raises up the NEEDY (ebyon) out of affliction' - the poor God exalts, the great reversal of the coda.
v42: 'The UPRIGHT (yashar) see it and are glad' - the just who rejoice to see God set things right.
v42: 'the upright see it and are GLAD (samach)' - the joy of the righteous at God's vindicating reversals.
v42: 'and all WICKEDNESS (evel) shuts its mouth' - the wicked struck dumb, evil silenced by God's justice.
v43: 'Whoever is WISE (chakam), let him attend to these things' - the wise who read God's dealings, the coda's charge.
v43: 'let him ATTEND (shamar) to these things' - the heeding of God's dealings, wisdom's task.
the steadfast love of the LORD
v43: 'let them CONSIDER (bin) the steadfast love of the LORD' - the discernment of God's covenant love in all his works, the psalm's closing wisdom.
